rationale: Tests recall of the nine essential amino acids from the complete set of twenty, anchored after the block that defines essential, semi-essential, ketogenic and glucogenic classifications.
Tests understanding of the four hierarchical levels of protein structure and their stabilising forces, anchored after the block that completes primary-to-quaternary organisation and denaturation.

Tests spatial identification of the four structural components of the IgG molecule, anchored after the block that describes Fab/Fc regions, heavy/light chains, complement activation and humoral versus cellular immunity.

Tests understanding of the proximal-to-distal sequence of protein digestion and absorption, anchored after the block that completes the zymogen cascade, enzyme specificities and transporter mechanisms.
Tests recall of key terms in ammonia metabolism and the urea cycle, anchored after the block that completes transamination, ammonia transport and the urea cycle enzymes and energetics.

Tests understanding of the multi-organ pathway of haem degradation from red cell destruction to faecal pigment, anchored after the block that completes haem synthesis, bilirubin metabolism and the van den Bergh reaction.

Tests recall of the key enzyme deficiencies and clinical features of the major inborn errors of amino acid metabolism, anchored after the block that completes PKU, alkaptonuria, homocystinuria, MSUD, Hartnup disease and newborn screening.

Tests recall of the molecular basis of haemoglobin structural variants and pathological derivatives, anchored after the block that completes HbS, HbE, thalassaemias, carboxyhaemoglobin, methaemoglobin and HbA1c.
